full_text:
Israel’s severe heat wave was already being felt across the country Saturday, a day before it was expected to reach its peak, with temperatures climbing above 40°C (104°F) in many inland areas.
The highest temperature was recorded at Gilgal in the Jordan Valley, where the mercury reached about 45.2°C (113.4°F). Temperatures rose to 43.5°C (110.3°F) at Capernaum on the northern shore of the Sea of Galilee, 42.5°C (108.5°F) in Tiberias and 43.5°C (110.3°F) in the Beit She’an area.
Dr. Amir Givati, director of the Israel Meteorological Service, said temperatures of 40°C (104°F) or higher were recorded across a broad stretch of the country, from Dafna near the northern border through the Hula Valley, Beit She’an Valley, Jordan Valley, Dead Sea and Arava regions, and as far south as Eilat.
Jerusalem reached 36.1°C (97°F), while temperatures in the Judean foothills climbed to about 40°C (104°F).
The coastal plain avoided the most extreme temperatures, with readings remaining near 30°C (86°F) because of the Mediterranean Sea. However, humidity levels of 70% to 75% created very high to extreme heat stress there as well.
The heat wave is expected to peak Sunday, with another rise in temperatures. Updated forecasts indicate temperatures could reach about 45°C (113°F) around the Sea of Galilee and between 46°C and 46.5°C (114.8°F to 115.7°F) in the Jordan Valley.
Despite the extreme heat, many Israelis spent Saturday outdoors. About 45,000 visitors entered nature reserves and national parks across the country, according to the Israel Nature and Parks Authority.
Water sites were the most popular destinations, led by Hurshat Tal, Gan HaShlosha, also known as the Sachne, and the Dor-Habonim Beach Nature Reserve. About 6,800 visitors stayed overnight at the authority’s campgrounds over the weekend, with Achziv Beach, Hurshat Tal, Ma’ayan Harod and Tel Ashkelon among the most popular sites.
Full forecast
Temperatures will rise again Sunday as Israel experiences the peak of the heat wave. Winds are expected to strengthen from the afternoon.
A slight drop in temperatures is forecast for Monday, although conditions will remain hotter than usual for the season and heavy heat stress will continue. Tuesday morning is expected to be clear, with a further decline in temperatures as the heat wave begins to ease.
Speaking to the ynet studio Thursday ahead of the heat wave, Givati urged the public to avoid outdoor activity during the hottest hours.
“This is an event of truly extreme heat,” he said. “There was a similar heat wave last August, and there were quite a few cases of heatstroke. Anyone in the Tel Aviv metropolitan area may not fully understand what we are talking about, but in the north it will be extremely hot and dry during the afternoon.”

The IMD on Saturday issued an ‘orange alert’ for 12 districts in Kerala, warning of very heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms on August 2, officials said.
The alert has been issued for Pathanamthitta, Alappuzha, Kottayam, Idukki, Ernakulam, Thrissur, Palakkad, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
An ‘orange alert’ indicates the likelihood of very heavy rainfall ranging from 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm in 24 hours at isolated places.
Heavy rain continued to trigger landslides and flooding across Kerala.
KSDMA advises vulnerable residents to move to safer places
The Kerala State Disaster Management Authority urged people living in areas prone to landslides, mudslides and flash floods to shift to safer locations if advised by the authorities.
Residents living along riverbanks and downstream of dams were advised to remain vigilant and relocate if directed by officials.
The KSDMA advised people in disaster-prone areas to ensure that relief camps had been opened in their localities and to move to them during the daytime if necessary.
It urged people living in weak or unsafe houses to remain cautious in view of the possibility of strong winds and shift to safer places if required.
Public urged to avoid risky travel and water bodies
The authority cautioned people against entering rivers, streams and other water bodies for bathing, fishing or crossing during the heavy rain.
It advised the public not to gather on bridges or attempt to take photographs or selfies near overflowing water bodies.
People have been urged to avoid all non-essential travel, particularly to hilly areas, waterfalls and reservoirs, until the weather warning is withdrawn.

Thiruvananthapuram: At least seven persons, including three children, were killed and many injured in rain-related calamities in various parts of Kerala since Friday night.

Minor landslides were reported in various parts of Idukki and Kottayam, while many areas of Pathanamthitta, Kozhikode, Wayanad and Malappuram were flooded.

A mother and son died at Poonjar in Kottayam district after their house collapsed in a landslide. Rajeena and her 24-year-old son Josephine were killed, while Rajeena's husband had a narrow escape.

Four-year-old Adam, son of Abdul Hameed and Nadeera of Kondotty in Malappuram, drowned in a swollen canal, while three-year-old Abdula Muhain, son of Abdul Muneer, drowned in a swollen canal at Wandoor in the district.

An 11-year-old boy, identified as Milan Shiju, drowned at Puthupally in Kottayam.

In the hilly district of Idukki, a woman identified as Sumathi died following a landslide at Adoormala. Another person, identified as Prabhakaran, died at Kolahalamedu in the district after the wall of a house collapsed.

Two fishermen are missing in the sea off the Muthalapozhi coast in Thiruvananthapuram after a boat capsized. The Coast Guard is carrying out the search.

.Central Kerala received exceptionally heavy rainfall, says KSDMA.

Many parts of Wayanad were also receiving heavy rain, leading to waterlogging. People living in calamity-prone areas were shifted to safer places. Landslips were also reported in the hilly areas of Kozhikode.

At Theekoyi in Kottayam district, four houses were destroyed in a landslide on Thursday night. Many people suffered injuries.

Many people stranded in houses in Ranni and Kozhencherry in Pathanamthitta following flash floods were being shifted to safe places using boats. These regions, which lie on the banks of the Pamba river, often witness flooding.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) sounded a red alert in eight districts across the state. Heavy winds are also forecast in many parts. High pressure variations and strong winds have caused heavy rain across the state. The rain is likely to subside by tomorrow.

Chief Minister V D Satheesan reviewed the situation and directed ministers in charge of each district to take necessary relief and precautionary measures.

The rains have also caused massive damage to crops.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red alert for six Gujarat districts, warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours, while indicating that rainfall activity across the state is likely to gradually ease from Sunday.
Six Districts Under Red Alert
Addressing the media, IMD Director AK Das said Morbi, Surendranagar, Ahmedabad, Rajkot, Botad and Bhavnagar have been placed under a red alert due to the likelihood of extremely heavy rainfall.
Orange and Yellow Alerts Issued
An orange alert has been issued for Banaskantha (Vav and Tharad), Patan, Mehsana, Sabarkantha, Aravalli, Gandhinagar, Kheda, Anand, Bharuch, Amreli, Jamnagar and Kutch, where heavy rainfall is expected at isolated places.
A yellow alert has been sounded for Devbhumi Dwarka, Porbandar, Junagadh, Gir Somnath, Diu, Mahisagar, Dahod, Panchmahal, Vadodara, Chhota Udepur, Narmada, Surat, Navsari, Valsad, Daman and Dadra & Nagar Haveli, with forecasts of isolated heavy rain.
Four Weather Systems Active
According to the IMD, the current spell is being driven by the combined influence of a well-marked low-pressure area, the monsoon trough, a shear zone and a western disturbance, resulting in widespread rainfall across Gujarat.
Fishermen Advised to Stay Ashore
The weather office has advised fishermen not to venture into the Arabian Sea until August 2 due to rough sea conditions. Signal No. 3 has also been hoisted at all ports along the Gujarat coast as a precaution.
Surendranagar Records Heavy Rain
Das said Surendranagar received 149.6 mm of rainfall, describing it as the district's fifth-highest recorded rainfall event.
The IMD added that Gujarat has received 439.9 mm of cumulative rainfall so far this monsoon season against the seasonal normal of 380.9 mm, representing 16% excess rainfall.
While the next 24 hours remain crucial for several districts, the IMD said rainfall intensity is expected to decrease from August 2, although isolated showers are likely to continue in parts of the state.
